MethodDescription: SiO2, Al2O3, Fe2O3, CaO, MgO, Na2O, K2O, Cr2O3, TiO2, MnO, P2O5, SrO, BaO, and LOI reported in weight percent. A calcined or ignited sample (0.9 g) is added to 9.0g of lithium borate flux (a solution of 50% lithium tetraborate and 50% lithium metaborate), mixed well and fused in an auto fluxer between 1050 - 1100°C. A flat molten glass disc is prepared from the resulting melt and the disc is then analyzed by X-ray Fluorescence Spectrometry (XRF). Loss on ignition (LOI) is determined by gravimetry as part of this process.

Ag, Ba, Ce, Co, Cr, Cs, Cu, Dy, Er, Eu, Ga, Gd, Hf, Ho, La, Lu, Mo, Nb, Nd, Ni, Pb, Pr, Rb, Sm, Sn, Sr, Ta, Tb, Th, Tl, Tm, U, V, W, Y, Yb, Zn, Zr, reported in parts per million by weight (ppm). A prepared sample (0.200 g) is added to lithium metaborate flux (0.90 g), mixed well and fused in a furnace at 1000°C. The resulting melt is then cooled and dissolved in 100 mL of 4% nitric acid / 2% hydrochloric acid solution. This solution is then analyzed by Inductively Coupled Plasma - Mass Spectrometry (ICP-MS).

Base metals Ag, As, Cd, Co, Cu, Li, Mo, Ni, Pb, Sc, Tl, Zn, reported in parts per million by weight (ppm). Sample preparation involves four-acid digestion of pulverized material utilizing a combination of nitric, perchloric, and hydrofluoric acids with a final dissolution stage using hydrochloric acid. This digestion breaks down most silicate and oxide minerals allowing for the “near-total” recovery of most minerals and analytes. The resulting material is analyzed by Inductively Coupled Plasma - Atomic Emission Spectroscopy (ICP-AES). Same as ME-4ACD81-2, plus Li, Tl.
